doc.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006

title: Musical families of New Orleans, the Jordan family
summary: Nearly every New Orleans family has musicians; he describes Kidd Jordan's family and the Chatiers family.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I don’t know if I’m all that well informed but it seems like for some reason the family connection in music is so strong in New Orleans.

It is very strong man, yeah. ‘Cause I was telling some of the students today that most everyone in New Orleans’ family, there’s somebody who plays music. Say for instance like Kidd Jordan, he’s here today with the New Orleans Jazz Camp, he has a son who plays flute, a son who plays trumpet, a daughter who plays the violin and another daughter who sings. And his other three kids, they have something to do with music but you know, they don’t play. The Jordan Family. And the kids married into the family called the Chatiers family in New Orleans with sixteen brothers and sisters and all of them played. Now in our jazz camp we have the young grandsons of those kids, they’re coming up, so it’s like the cycle is moving on. Whether they become professional musicians, we don’t know, because they’re like eight, nine, ten years old. But they’re being exposed to it. If they want it, it’s there.
